reviews.text: [h1][b]摇或死：塞入武器筹码，凭概率的天算，我们转出一条生路[/b][/h1] 肉鸽like（或者lite）赛道已日渐臃肿，带肥的还有各路子赛道，比如说，本作《Slot or Not》的肉鸽老虎机玩法游戏，虽然本作没有革新这种玩法的框架，但是游玩前期，鉴于武器即便不组流派就有一定实力，所以会有一定通宵达命的动力，毕竟谁不喜欢纯粹概率博弈中胜利的天平可以通过人力慢慢拨弄到玩家自己身边呢。 [h2][b]投币-旋转-结算：用概率战胜对手[/b][/h2] 如果说《杀戮尖塔》《炉石传说》这类游戏需要玩家精算才能力避伏笔，那么本作其实和毁誉或参半的《竞拍之王》一样，再完成攻击结算前，一切交给天命，只有打开盒子/老虎机摇臂结算后，才知道[b]薛定谔的猫是死还是生。[/b] 唯一需要玩家考虑的，是针对底部的出牌槽，计算≤行动点的出牌（武器），然后放到奖池里面，武器一般分为三类，[b]攻击的大类[/b]有侧重攻击频率增加的，也有挂负面比如流血中毒的，也有AOE的；[b]防御的大类[/b]主要侧重于提供当前回合的临时护甲，类似《月圆之夜》的互动；[b]增益大类中[/b]大部分是回血的，这些血包物件大部分都是耗品，一旦放入奖池就会消失。 [b]所以游戏并没有特别讲求大小卡组的增删，玩家想要玩大卡组，就不要选即时使用的耗品；[/b]想要精选小卡组，就拿好核心武器之后，多选用完即丢的物品或者干脆看到每一关通过后的奖励，选择跳过即可。 [b]因为精选卡组完全不如祈祷每回合老虎机给个好结果[/b]，当我们放入这些物件之后，我们就能看到在老虎机的抽选概率下，自己的某道具被抽到的概率是多少，敌人的障碍模块被抽到的概率是多少，有时候[b]敌人的下一轮行动也会破坏掉老虎机的某一个单元格[/b]，但再怎么尽人事，最终都得听天命。 在三选一武器的时候，[b]可能会有流派构筑的大致方向，但是大部分时候还是会选择高罕且明显强力的武器[/b]，期望的计算固然可以让每一回合的攻击稍微有精算感，但是赌上限才是老虎机玩法最本真之处（bushi）。 老虎机会随着肉鸽爬塔而不断膨胀，从一开始的3*1到矩形不断扩增，如无其他局内天赋，玩家只会在三连的时候收获爆炸增益（BOOST），即同名武器造成的伤害有倍增，所以有时候多选重复武器也是一个好思路。[b]当然，随着我们在商店/奖励关获得其他局内增益，我们会获得不同的爆炸增益的触发条件，斜连的二格、横向的四格都可以连携打出大伤害，此时，老虎机会逐渐适应渐难的地图关卡。[/b] [h2][b]丰富的局内构筑与有待加强的局外增益[/b][/h2] 有创意连携，以及敌人与老虎机的互动，但是本作没有跳脱出老虎机肉鸽的核心思路——特定构筑达成之后玩家会以来这些强者恒强的方法论，后期复玩的时候玩家可能会偏想如何进一步达成上一轮的强力组件，而不是《大巴扎》式的，用新一轮的全新开局，让你多试不同流派，虽然随着BOSS通过，精英怪击败，能解锁新主控角色与新武器，但大部分情况下，如果在第二张地图开始碰壁，第三章地图带来的失败可能性就比较大。 除此之外，创意与画风符合一个甜品小独游应有的所有要素，如有中文，感兴趣的朋友不妨一试。 [quote]欢迎关注 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45531068/]黑白测评[/url] [hr]黑夜显真 白昼辨伪

Slot or Not offers fantastic replay value. Every run feels fresh thanks to the variety of items and the different enemy types you encounter along the way. There are also different characters, skins, and item gems here. Progression system feels rewarding, and learning how to manipulate the slot mechanics to your advantage is highly engaging. Its a beautifully crafted game that respects the players time

I enjoyed my first plays of Slot or Not. It combines the human urge to gamble with the strategery of roguelikes of choosing what upgrades you want to flesh out your build. I enjoyed the graphics, which includes filters to mimic VHS and old CRT monitors. That being said, I had the most issue with the Cayman fight in the 2nd area: one of his attacks turns the screen pink and activates a 'drunk' filter that when combined, hurts my eyes. I had to look away from the screen for minutes at a time to let my head settle before I could even continue the fight. As far as mechanics go, everything is spelled out in the in-game manual. I like experiencing the game without having to go read. It's overwhelming, but I think it's better to use it to figure out what went wrong during a run. (My suggestion is to add a death recap: died to bleed/poison/etc) so it's easier to look up details instead of poring over pages of text and reading everything at once.) Hopefully I can have enough time to play more later. As far as game mechanics, everything is solid and holds my attention. Though, I'd like to see some sort of other systems in it. I'm unsure what to add, though, since it's polished and finished. Overall, it's enjoyable and worth playing. I can fully recommend Slot or Not, despite the few complaints about graphics and text overload that I have.

Echoing the sentiment of many other reviewers, I wish steam allows us to give a 'neutral' review. Please look at my review less as a 'I hate this game' and more like a 'I cannot recommend it at its current state'. The core idea and loop of the gameplay is solid. It's not the first of its kind, but it does it well, and it does have its own share of novel mechanics like the increasing rows and columns of the slots. However, the problem comes in two things: 1. The balancing. The appeal of Slay the Spire is that you are in full control of your attacks and defences. You can count, you can plan based on enemy patterns. However, in Slot or Not, that goes slightly out the window because the damage and defence is random. You might put in 3 defences each giving possibly 2-4, and you might have a 4x4 grid which means your chance of getting enough is quite high, but it all can go out the window because of bad RNG, meanwhile the enemies always hits the same amount (and they get stronger ever act). That's fine, that's the core of the game, it's quite literally gambling. It's shown in how some weapons' effect are percentage based like the 25% echo hammer or the 25% ricochet on guns. It becomes an issue because it's combined with problem 2: there's not enough content. The '?' event nodes in the game is mostly just spin the wheel. Unlike StS that has narrative-driven choices of do A or B and get X or Y which can enrich and change your playstyle, all you get is a spin the wheel or a trade-up. And because this stays the same even when you progress to another act, the world feels dry and dead. I get the same events on the last act as I did on the first act! Not to mention the lack of variety of builds. You have damage, defence, poison, bleed, heal. That's it. No unique system, no unique buff/debuffs aside from boosting your slots, which forces you then to save and buy only the slot-boos trinkets. To make matter worse, there's only a few items that has inherent bleed/poison, and all the heals are consumables (unless you get lucky with a modifier on your cards). The whole core and lifeblood of the game is that it's all gambling, it's all gacha and they lean into it and it's fun... for awhile. When you progress to later acts you realize if you want to win you have to skew the odds in your favor, so you have to min-max everything, and that's just how these games goes. The issue with SoN is that due to the balancing problem and the lack of content problem, the game becomes tedious. Slow, careful gameplay is rewarded, while enemies increasingly become bullet sponges, which means every enemy node takes longer and longer. I'll say it again. The game is tedious. Especially during the final two acts. That's the biggest issue. Once I'm 70% through the run my build is complete and I CAN'T add anything new because all the things I can add will only subtract from my build. If I want to reliably win I have to skew the odds into my favour, but right now there is so little content and agency that is provided to the player that I am railroaded to do only a few 'safe' builds to reliably win. There is no high risk high reward build that can truly work because the variety of the builds are so much lesser compared to other games in this genre. This game feels like it's early access in terms of amount of content. It took me only 2.7 hours to win against the last boss, and there's no progression after that. I would say give it a few months to cook in the oven before buying. I definitely will wait a year to see if any sizable content comes up before attempting another run. I hope it gets better, because the core idea is fun.

Slot or Not is an inventive roguelike strategy game developed by MakoTeam and published by Proteus Interactive that takes two seemingly incompatible ideas—slot machines and deck-building combat—and merges them into a surprisingly cohesive experience. Instead of relying on traditional cards or turn-based attacks alone, the game builds its entire combat system around a customizable battle slot machine. The result is a colorful adventure that combines calculated decision-making with moments of suspense, creating a gameplay loop that feels fresh even within a genre crowded by countless roguelike releases. The game follows Bun Dorian, a quick-witted hare who finds himself facing an unusual crisis. His homeland is threatened by an army of aggressive and bizarre fruit creatures, and his greatest ally is not a sword, magical artifact, or legendary warrior, but a sentient slot machine named Slottie. This eccentric premise immediately establishes the playful personality of the game. Rather than taking itself too seriously, Slot or Not embraces its quirky world and uses humor to create a setting that feels memorable and distinct from more conventional fantasy adventures. Combat serves as the heart of the experience and is where the game's creativity shines brightest. Every encounter revolves around spinning Slottie's reels, with each symbol representing weapons, abilities, defenses, or special effects. At first glance, success may appear heavily dependent on luck, but deeper play reveals a system built around preparation and strategic planning. Players gradually fill their inventory with new equipment and modifiers that influence future spins, allowing them to manipulate probabilities and construct highly specialized builds. The excitement comes from watching carefully assembled strategies come together when the reels align perfectly during battle. What makes the gameplay particularly satisfying is the large number of synergies available. Different items can interact in unexpected ways, producing combinations that dramatically alter combat performance. Some builds focus on overwhelming offensive power, while others emphasize survival, status effects, or resource generation. Discovering these combinations becomes one of the most rewarding aspects of the game. Every successful run feels partially shaped by skillful planning and partially by adapting to whatever opportunities the game presents along the way. The roguelike structure ensures strong replay value. Procedurally generated encounters, randomized rewards, and varying item availability mean that each journey unfolds differently. Players are constantly encouraged to adapt their strategies based on what they find rather than relying on a single dominant approach. This unpredictability keeps the experience engaging over multiple runs, as every playthrough presents new possibilities and challenges. Even failed attempts rarely feel wasted because they often reveal new strategies or combinations worth exploring in future runs. A major strength of Slot or Not is its progression system. The abundance of items, trinkets, and equipment creates a constant sense of discovery. New rewards frequently have the potential to reshape an entire build, encouraging experimentation rather than repetition. Because powerful combinations can emerge from unexpected sources, players are motivated to try unusual strategies and take calculated risks. This design philosophy gives the game a strong sense of variety and helps prevent the gameplay from becoming stale. The presentation complements the mechanics exceptionally well. The game's hand-drawn visual style is vibrant, expressive, and full of charm. Characters possess distinctive personalities, while enemy designs embrace the absurdity of the game's premise. The invading fruit creatures are both amusing and creative, helping establish a world that feels unique despite its relatively simple narrative framework. The colorful environments and smooth animations ensure that every battle remains visually entertaining, even during longer play sessions. Audio design also contributes significantly to the game's appeal. The energetic soundtrack reinforces the lighthearted tone and keeps the pace moving during combat encounters. Sound effects associated with spinning reels, successful combinations, and powerful attacks provide satisfying feedback that makes every victory feel earned. Together, the music and audio cues help maintain excitement throughout the adventure without becoming repetitive. One of the game's greatest achievements is its accessibility. The basic concept is immediately understandable, allowing new players to jump into the action without extensive tutorials. At the same time, the underlying systems contain enough depth to satisfy experienced roguelike enthusiasts. This balance between simplicity and complexity allows the game to appeal to a broad audience while still rewarding those who invest time in mastering its mechanics. Its primary weakness stems from the very mechanic that makes it unique. Although player decisions significantly influence outcomes, randomness remains a central component of every battle. Players who prefer entirely deterministic strategy games may occasionally find the unpredictability frustrating. However, the game generally succeeds in ensuring that luck enhances tension rather than completely determining success, making most defeats feel like opportunities to improve rather than unfair setbacks. Slot or Not is a clever and highly entertaining roguelike that demonstrates how innovative design can breathe new life into familiar genres. By transforming a slot machine into a strategic combat system and surrounding it with rewarding progression, imaginative visuals, and substantial replayability, MakoTeam has created an experience that feels genuinely distinctive. Its combination of creativity, charm, and strategic depth makes it one of the more memorable indie roguelikes in recent years and a worthwhile recommendation for players seeking something refreshingly different. Rating: 8/10

游戏流程就是搜集具有良好随机词条的道具，偶尔去商店购买具有被动效果的神器，以及花越来越贵的价钱删道具。除此以外就没有任何能够提升强化牌组的方式。道具没法强化，道具间的配合也没有，只有随机词条可能有一点道具间的联动。总的来说，游戏构筑太浅，基本就是堆数值。 怪物种类很少，同一大关，路上的小怪都是一样的。 怪物机制也没什么特色，大部分怪物攻击方式都没什么差异，只有血量伤害方面的数值变化。 连续的相同的小怪战斗真的很无聊，得不到什么提升，打小怪只是为了拿金币。 地图设计也很垃圾，我不明白“单节点后面分出三条岔路，但这三条岔路都是通向小怪节点，然后连接到同一个单节点”这种地图分叉有什么意义，不同的选择有任何区别吗？看似地图随机需要规划路线增加重玩价值，实则徒有其表东施效颦。 遇到箱子必须拿道具，最多只能花钱roll，无论如何，都必须向牌组中添加一个道具，这种强行臃肿牌组的事件，我宁愿选择不去。 真的很无聊。

Slot or Not is a really enjoyable game with great visuals and a great overall gameplay feel. All the animations, sounds, and the general feeling of the game are genuinely very satisfying The core idea of the game also is alright, you put random items into a slot machine and random things happen, but you still have some level of control over it However, at times the game feels far too random. For example, after winning a fight, you get the classic modern roguelike "choice of three" items to add to your deck. The problem is that not only are the items random, but they also have random modifiers. I once got a healing item that rolled a modifier which made it deal damage to me, so the item was completely useless Apart from the randomness, which is sometimes fun but sometimes overdone, I feel like the game is missing more synergy. There are not many things that meaningfully work together. Of course, there are conditions like “if this item is next to another item,” but that still feels random. The trinkets you can buy in the shop mostly focus on basic increases, like boosting the multiplier or damage. I miss the feeling of building around a specific strategy I completed one run by simply choosing the options with the highest numbers. Out of around 30 item choices, I skipped about 3/4 of them because I already had one item that I could just keep putting into the machine and watch the multipliers spin while dealing 400 damage The game is really enjoyable, but I am not sure whether I would want to come back to it after finishing it once. Still, it is worth its price, and the animations and effects are genuinely beautiful I would focus on adding more variety and creativity in how items and trinkets interact with each other
